results.title: Fixed vs Variable Costs: How to Evaluate Trade-Offs
results.content: # How do you evaluate the trade-off between fixed and variable costs in different scenarios and contexts? What are fixed and variable costs? In this article, you will learn how to evaluate the trade-off between fixed and variable costs in different scenarios and contexts, and how to apply some useful tools and techniques to optimize your cost structure and performance. ## 1 What are fixed and variable costs? Variable costs are expenses that change in proportion to the level of production or sales. On the other hand, fixed costs are expenses that remain constant regardless of the level of production or sales. - Fixed Costs: These are expenses that remain constant regardless of production levels, such as rent, salaries, and insurance. The trade-off between fixed and variable costs affects the profitability, risk, and flexibility of a business. A high fixed cost structure means that the business has a high break-even point, but also a high operating leverage, which means that a small change in sales can result in a large change in profits. A high variable cost structure means that the business has a low break-even point, but also a low operating leverage, which means that a large change in sales can result in a small change in profits. One way to analyze the trade-off between fixed and variable costs is to use the contribution margin ratio, which is the percentage of sales that remains after deducting variable costs. Another way to optimize the trade-off between fixed and variable costs is to use the target costing method, which is a technique that sets the desired selling price and profit margin for a product or service, and then works backward to determine the maximum allowable cost. Finally, it is important to recognize that the optimal trade-off between fixed and variable costs may vary depending on different scenarios and contexts, such as the industry, the product life cycle, the competitive advantage, the demand uncertainty, and the strategic goals of the business. In engineering project management, assessing the trade-off between fixed and variable costs involves analyzing upfront investments versus ongoing operational expenses. ## More articles on Cost Control.

results.title: MambaOcc: Visual State Space Model for BEV-based Occupancy Prediction with Local Adaptive Reordering
results.content: # MambaOcc: Visual State Space Model for BEV-based Occupancy Prediction with Local Adaptive Reordering. To address these challenges, in this paper, we propose a Mamba-based occupancy prediction method (MambaOcc) adopting BEV features to ease the burden of 3D scenario representation, and linear Mamba-style attention to achieve efficient long-range perception. Occupancy prediction, Mamba, State space model, Bird’s eye view. Occupancy prediction involves determining the state of every voxel in a 3D scenario, which results in high computational and memory demands during the development of perception models. While it demonstrates promising results for efficient occupancy prediction, its performance heavily depends on powerful 2D backbones like Transformers [4]. To this end, we propose MambaOcc, a novel occupancy prediction method based on the Mamba framework, designed to be lightweight while providing efficient long-range modeling. To mitigate the high computational burden associated with 3D voxels, we use BEV features as the intermediate representation for occupancy prediction and develop a hybrid BEV encoder combining convolutional layers and Mamba layers. A lightweight Mamba-based occupancy prediction method (MambaOcc) is proposed, which boosts the performance of the BEV-based approach with significantly less computation cost. A novel LAR-SS2D hybrid encoder with the local adaptive reordering mechanism is proposed, which enables more flexible sequence order optimization and improves the performance of state space models. FlashOCC [3] introduced a BEV-based 3D representation method for fast and memory-efficient occupancy prediction while maintaining high precision. In this section, we will elaborate on the proposed MambaOcc from four aspects: The Mamba-based image backbone (VM-Backbone) for image feature extraction, view transformation and temporal fusion module to obtain BEV-format features and aggregate multi-frame features, LAR-SS2D hybrid BEV encoder with the adaptive local re-ordering module, and the occupancy prediction head. Table III presents the impact of different initialization methods for the image backbone on occupancy prediction performance. In this paper, we propose the first Mamba-based occupancy prediction network, named MambaOcc. Thanks to Mamba’s linear attention mechanism and long-range context modeling approach, MambaOcc surpasses CNN-based methods while offering higher parameter efficiency compared to Transformer-based approaches. Zhang, “Voxel mamba: Group-free state space models for point cloud based 3d object detection,” *arXiv preprint arXiv:2406.10700*, 2024.

results.title: A lightweight Dual-Stream Attention Network for real-time landslide monitoring in multi-modal remote sensing imagery - ScienceDirect
results.content: # A lightweight Dual-Stream Attention Network for real-time landslide monitoring in multi-modal remote sensing imagery. Rapid delineation of landslides from post-event remote-sensing imagery demands models that can be *deployed in the field*, often on battery-powered edge devices with strict memory and latency budgets. We therefore introduce a *Dual-Stream Attention Network* whose total trainable footprint is just *2.03* M parameters – roughly the size of a single JPEG image – yet still exploits the complementary physics of co-registered RGB orthomosaics and digital-elevation models. Ablation studies show that each architectural choice – dual-stream processing, late fusion, and attentional gating – contributes at least pp IoU. The Dual-Stream Attention Network advances landslide segmentation through four tightly-coupled innovations: (i) *modality-disentangled encoders* and that generate orthogonal feature subspaces , safeguarding spectral texture and DEM-derived information before cross-modal interference; (ii) a *scale-adaptive encoder–decoder backbone* in which each level applies the composite operator (with convolution and non-parametric pooling), thereby achieving equivariance to -pixel dilations while keeping the network’s Lipschitz constant bounded; (iii) a *gradient-stable attention gate* that modulates skip-features under the contractive constraint , thus focusing computation on landslide-salient regions without jeopardising optimisation; and (iv) an *end-to-end fusion decoder* learned directly from data and containing only parameters, which obviates heuristic feature engineering while retaining universal approximation capability. first demonstrated that landslide susceptibility can be modelled through discriminant analysis once lithology, relief and hydrology are encoded in a geographical information system (GIS) (Guzzetti et al., 2002, Guzzetti et al., 1999). Table 3, Table 4, Table 5, Table 6 evaluate the proposed *Dual-Stream* architecture against a spectrum of ImageNet-initialised backbones on two independent landslide corpora and for two tasks—tile-level detection and pixel-level segmentation. We presented a rigorously derived *Dual-Stream Attention Network* that keeps the entire trainable footprint to **2.03 M** parameters – less than 5% of a typical DeepLabv3+ backbone – while still exploiting the complementary physics of co-registered RGB orthomosaics and DEM-derived slope break. ### Conv-trans dual network for landslide detection of multi-channel optical remote sensing images. ### A globally distributed dataset of coseismic landslide mapping via multi-source high-resolution remote sensing images. ### Landslide mapping using two main deep-learning convolution neural network streams combined by the Dempster–Shafer model. ### EMR-HRNet: A multi-scale feature fusion network for landslide segmentation from remote sensing images.

results.title: [PDF] Context-aware Image Compression Optimization for Visual Analytics ...
results.content: This paper presents CICO, a Context-aware Image Compression Optimization framework to achieve low-bandwidth and low-latency visual analytics offload-ing. CICO is a lightweight frame-work that contextualizes and optimizes image compression for low-bandwidth and low-latency visual analytics offloading in vision apps. By putting the compression of each image region under a vision app into a context, CICO is able to minimize the required network bandwidth for visual analytics offloading while preserv-ing the analytics accuracy. By comparing CICO with traditional JPEG standard and a CNN-based compression method [43], our extensive results demonstrate that CICO improves the accuracy-bandwidth trade-offs of JPEG and CNN-based encoders and achieves a lower end-to-end latency and higher processing speed for visual analytics offloading.

results.title: EdgeCodec: Onboard Lightweight High Fidelity Neural Compressor with Residual Vector Quantization
results.content: We address this issue by compressing local data using a neural network supplemented with the Residual Vector Quantization (RVQ) technique. Even though data compression is an active area of research within IoT [10], its deployment and application remains limited due to the lack of lightweight compression libraries able to run at the edge on resource constrained MCUs. The main challenge comes from the limited availability of onboard computation power and memory [11, 12] since most compression algorithms are designed for high-end platforms, such as smartphones [4, 5]. Thus, there is a need for lightweight and efficient lossy compression algorithms specifically targeted for low-power IoT devices, typically featuring MCUs with a total memory in the range of \qty1\megaB. A trade-off between CR and compression quality exists; in our field tests, we noticed an average error on the reconstructed data between 2.5% and 2.9%, depending on the selected CR, values always within the application specification of 3% discussed in Section II-B. In detail, this paper’s main contributions are: (i) A novel lightweight lossy compressor for multi-channel time-series data, named EdgeCodec, specifically designed for low-power IoT devices. Nowadays, with the new advent of Edge computing [16], new lossy compression algorithms can be developed for low power and resource constrained IoT sensor nodes [16], exploiting ML techniques to reach high CR () at low latency and low computational effort. It employs a streaming encoder-decoder architecture with a quantized latent space, trained end-to-end to achieve efficient and high-quality audio compression [5]. This study builds its foundation on the concept brought by EnCodec and SoundStream, an end-to-end neural compression with residual vector quantization and an adversarial neural network used during training, to develop an Edge computing compatible lossy encoder for multi-channel time-series bitstreams. (ii) The Residual Vector Quantizer, which further transforms (compresses) the input latent representation to N bits via a finite set of codebooks, where each of them represents a quantized value of each dimension of the latent space. In practice, the RVQ is essential to deploy an efficient compressor at the edge; a single quantization layer would need a very large (indeed, exponentially large) codebook to represent the compressed data accurately.
